vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: furry-art-skill
Version: 1.6.0

The skill is a straightforward wrapper for the Neta/TalesOfAI image generation API. The Node.js script (furryart.js) takes a user prompt, sends it to a legitimate API endpoint (api.talesofai.cn), and polls for the resulting image URL. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious instructions in the documentation.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a furry-image generator that uses an external API, but there are multiple mismatches between its documentation, manifest, and code (token handling and target API host) that warrant caution before installing or giving it a token.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included code (an image-generation client). Requesting a NETA token is reasonable for that purpose. However, the README/SKILL.md point to Neta (neta.art) while the code calls api.talesofai.cn/oss.talesofai.cn — a domain mismatch that should be explained by the author.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README instruct users to provide NETA_TOKEN; some snippets show passing it via --token which matches the script, but README claims the script will look for NETA_TOKEN environment variable as fallback — the actual code does NOT read process.env.NETA_TOKEN and will exit if --token isn't provided. This inconsistency could cause accidental token exposure or failed runs and suggests the docs were not updated to match the code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and only a small JS script are included. No remote downloads or package installs are performed by the skill itself, which reduces installation risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a single credential (NETA_TOKEN) is required, which is proportional. But registry metadata reported no required env vars while package.json's clawhub metadata marks NETA_TOKEN as required — this mismatch is confusing. Also the script sends the token to api.talesofai.cn; you should confirm that this is the legitimate Neta backend before providing secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and has no install hooks that modify system or other skills. It does not request persistent elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a small Node CLI that submits text prompts to an external image API and prints back an image URL. Before installing or supplying your NETA_TOKEN, verify: (1) which host the token is actually sent to — the code targets api.talesofai.cn (not neta.art), so confirm that talesofai.cn is an official Neta endpoint; (2) prefer passing a temporary or limited-scope token via the --token flag rather than storing a long-lived token in an environment file; (3) ask the author to fix the documentation vs. code mismatches (package.json/README claim env fallback that the script does not implement); (4) run the script in an isolated environment (no sensitive files open) and monitor network traffic the first time to ensure the endpoint and payload are expected. The inconsistencies look like sloppy packaging rather than outright malicious behavior, but they increase risk because you may accidentally send secrets to an unexpected host.
